## ForceConnect 2.1.2 — auto-update is on

> **2.1.2** is the first signed release, so **auto-update works from this version on**. ForceConnect checks for a new release at launch (turn that off in **Settings → Updates**) and installs it only when you click **Install**. Every update is verified against ForceConnect's signing key before anything is written to disk.
>
> **Install this one by hand.** Earlier versions (2.0 to 2.1.1) can't verify updates, so they won't offer this release automatically. Once you're on 2.1.2, later versions arrive by themselves. Your settings and custom servers are kept.

ForceConnect 2.1 brings the app to **macOS and Linux** for the first time, adds a **compact window**, and lets you decide **where your DNS goes when you disconnect**.

### ✨ What's new

- **macOS and Linux (beta)** — ForceConnect now runs on all three desktop platforms. See the beta note below before you install.
- **Default DNS** — choose an everyday DNS server in **Settings → When you disconnect**. ForceConnect switches to it whenever you disconnect, and when the app closes, so you're never dropped back onto your provider's DNS.
- **Restore previous DNS** — ForceConnect saves the DNS your system had when it started and puts exactly that back when you disconnect. It's on by default. Turn both options off to go back to automatic (DHCP) DNS instead.
- **Crash-safe, too** — whichever option you pick also applies after a crash, a forced shutdown or a power loss.
- **Compact mode** — a small 360×450 window with just the essentials: connection status, the power button, the server picker, latency and your adapter. Open it from the new button in the title bar or from Settings. You can pin it on top of other windows, and ForceConnect remembers which mode you left it in.
- **Lighter in compact mode** — the live latency graph and server-list checks stop, refreshes slow down, animations are switched off, and the app asks the web engine to keep its memory use low.
- **Simpler "Add server" dialog** — enter the IP addresses once. Add an encrypted address if you want one, and the same IPs are used to reach it.

### 🧪 macOS and Linux are in beta

The macOS and Linux builds are **new and have not been tested on real machines yet**. They may not work, or may not work fully.

**Please try them and tell me how it goes:** [open an issue](https://github.com/Mxqius/ForceConnect/issues/new) with your OS version, what you tried, and what happened — screenshots and error messages help a lot. Reports that everything works are just as useful.

- **macOS:** the app isn't notarized yet. On first launch, right-click ForceConnect and choose **Open**, or allow it under **System Settings → Privacy & Security**. You'll be asked for your password once, when the app starts.
- **Linux:** needs NetworkManager or systemd-resolved to change DNS, and polkit for the password prompt, which appears once, when the app starts.

### 📥 Download

| Platform         | File                                                              | Requirements                                        |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| **Windows**      | `ForceConnect_2.1.2_x64-setup.exe`                                | Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) or later, x64 |
| **macOS** (beta) | `ForceConnect_2.1.2_universal.dmg`                                | macOS 10.15 or later, Apple Silicon or Intel        |
| **Linux** (beta) | `.deb` (Debian, Ubuntu), `.rpm` (Fedora, openSUSE) or `.AppImage` | NetworkManager or systemd-resolved, and polkit      |

### ⚠️ Good to know

- **Windows SmartScreen** may warn that the installer is from an unrecognized publisher, because it isn't code-signed yet. Click **More info → Run anyway**.
- **Updating from 2.0, 2.1.0 or 2.1.1** means installing this version manually, once. After that, updates install from inside the app.

### 🐞 Feedback

Found a bug or want a DNS provider added? [Open an issue](https://github.com/Mxqius/ForceConnect/issues). Adding a provider needs no Rust — just edit [`servers.json`](https://github.com/Mxqius/ForceConnect/blob/main/src-tauri/crates/dns/servers.json).
